title: Three Visitors; Abraham Pleads for Sodom

verses.text: Then the LORD appeared to Abraham by the Oaks of Mamre in the heat of the day, while he was sitting at the entrance of his tent.
And Abraham looked up and saw three men standing nearby. When he saw them, he ran from the entrance of his tent to meet them and bowed low to the ground.
"My lord," said Abraham, "if I have found favor in your sight, please do not pass your servant by.
Let a little water be brought, that you may wash your feet and rest yourselves under the tree.

And I will bring a bit of bread so that you may refresh yourselves. This is why you have passed your servant's way. After that, you may continue on your way." "Yes," they replied, "you may do as you have said."
So Abraham hurried into the tent and said to Sarah, "Quick! Prepare three seahs of fine flour, knead it, and bake some bread."
Meanwhile, Abraham ran to the herd, selected a tender and choice calf, and gave it to a servant, who hurried to prepare it.
Then Abraham brought curds and milk and the calf that had been prepared, and he set them before the men and stood by them under the tree as they ate.
"Where is your wife Sarah?" they asked. "There, in the tent," he replied.
Then the LORD said, "I will surely return to you at this time next year, and your wife Sarah will have a son!" Now Sarah was behind him, listening at the entrance to the tent.
And Abraham and Sarah were already old and well along in years; Sarah had passed the age of childbearing.
So she laughed to herself, saying, "After I am worn out and my master is old, will I now have this pleasure?"
And the LORD asked Abraham, "Why did Sarah laugh and say, 'Can I really bear a child when I am old?'
Is anything too difficult for the LORD? At the appointed time I will return to you—in about a year—and Sarah will have a son."
But Sarah was afraid, so she denied it and said, "I did not laugh." "No," replied the LORD, "but you did laugh."
When the men got up to leave, they looked out over Sodom, and Abraham walked along with them to see them off.
And the LORD said, "Shall I hide from Abraham what I am about to do?
Abraham will surely become a great and powerful nation, and through him all the nations of the earth will be blessed.

For I have chosen him, so that he will command his children and his household after him to keep the way of the LORD by doing what is right and just, in order that the LORD may bring upon Abraham what He has promised."
Then the LORD said, "The outcry against Sodom and Gomorrah is great. Because their sin is so grievous,
I will go down to see if their actions fully justify the outcry that has reached Me. If not, I will find out."
And the two men turned away and went toward Sodom, but Abraham remained standing before the LORD.
Abraham stepped forward and said, "Will You really sweep away the righteous with the wicked?
What if there are fifty righteous ones in the city? Will You really sweep it away and not spare the place for the sake of the fifty righteous ones who are there?

Far be it from You to do such a thing—to kill the righteous with the wicked, so that the righteous and the wicked are treated alike. Far be it from You! Will not the Judge of all the earth do what is right?"
So the LORD replied, "If I find fifty righteous ones within the city of Sodom, on their account I will spare the whole place."
Then Abraham answered, "Now that I have ventured to speak to the Lord—though I am but dust and ashes—
suppose the fifty righteous ones lack five. Will You destroy the whole city for the lack of five?" He replied, "If I find forty-five there, I will not destroy it."
Once again Abraham spoke to the LORD, "Suppose forty are found there?" He answered, "On account of the forty, I will not do it."
Then Abraham said, "May the Lord not be angry, but let me speak further. Suppose thirty are found there?" He replied, "If I find thirty there, I will not do it."
And Abraham said, "Now that I have ventured to speak to the Lord, suppose twenty are found there?" He answered, "On account of the twenty, I will not destroy it."
Finally, Abraham said, "May the Lord not be angry, but let me speak once more. Suppose ten are found there?" And He answered, "On account of the ten, I will not destroy it."
When the LORD had finished speaking with Abraham, He departed, and Abraham returned home.

context.author: Genesis names no author. Jewish and Christian tradition, and the New Testament’s way of speaking of “the Law of Moses” (Luke 24:44), credit the five books of the Law to Moses. Many scholars think Genesis was gathered and shaped from older sources over a long time, and a few remarks look back from a later day: “at that time the Canaanites were in the land” (Genesis 12:6).
context.genre: Family narrative: the story of Abraham, Sarah and their family (Genesis 11:27 to 25:11)
context.audience: Israel, the children of Abraham, learning how God’s promise began
context.setting: “The LORD appeared to Abraham by the Oaks of Mamre in the heat of the day, while he was sitting at the entrance of his tent” (v.1). He sees three men, runs to meet them, bows, and hurries to serve them bread, a tender calf, curds and milk under the tree (vv.2-8). They ask, “Where is your wife Sarah?” and the LORD says, “your wife Sarah will have a son!” (vv.9-10). Sarah, listening at the tent door, laughs to herself; the LORD asks, “Why did Sarah laugh?… Is anything too difficult for the LORD?” (vv.12-14). She denies it out of fear, and the LORD answers, “but you did laugh” (v.15). As the men set out toward Sodom, the LORD says, “Shall I hide from Abraham what I am about to do?” (v.17), and tells him the outcry against Sodom is great (vv.20-21). Abraham steps forward: “Will You really sweep away the righteous with the wicked?… Will not the Judge of all the earth do what is right?” (vv.23-25). He bargains from fifty righteous down to ten, and the LORD agrees: “On account of the ten, I will not destroy it” (v.32).
context.custom: Hospitality to strangers was a sacred duty in the desert, where a traveler without shelter or water could die. A host ran to meet guests, washed their feet, killed an animal (a rare thing, since flocks were wealth) and stood by while they ate (v.8). Abraham offers “a bit of bread” (v.5) and serves a feast: three seahs of flour, about 20 liters. Bargaining back and forth, as in the market, was the ordinary way to reach agreement.
context.timelineImmediate: Chapter 19 tells how the two angels came to Sodom, rescued Lot and his daughters, and the LORD destroyed the cities.
context.timelineBible: Hebrews says, “Do not neglect to show hospitality to strangers, for by so doing some people have entertained angels without knowing it” (Hebrews 13:2). When the angel tells Mary of Elizabeth’s child in her old age, he answers the same doubt: “For no word from God will ever fail” (Luke 1:37). Jesus said it would be more bearable for Sodom on the day of judgment than for the towns that saw His miracles and did not repent (Matthew 11:23-24). Andrei Rublev’s icon of the three visitors became the best-known Christian image of the Trinity.

translation.meaning: To laugh. The root of Isaac’s name, Yitschaq, ‘he laughs.’ Both Abraham (17:17) and Sarah laugh at the promise.
To be wonderful, extraordinary, too hard. The same root is used of God’s ‘wonders.’
To judge, govern, set right. Abraham appeals to God as the Judge of all the earth, who must do justice.

gospelParallels.note: Some have entertained angels without knowing it.
No word from God will ever fail.
He did not waver in unbelief at the promise of God.

otBackground.note: Nothing is too difficult for You.
The LORD is righteous in all His ways.
If you can find a single person who acts justly, I will forgive her.

overview.summary: The LORD and two angels visit Abraham at Mamre; he serves them a feast, and the LORD promises that Sarah will have a son within a year, though she laughs; then Abraham pleads with the LORD for Sodom, down to ten righteous people.
overview.settingLine: The tent at Mamre in the heat of the day.

customs.t: The first kindness to a traveler.
The ordinary way to reach terms.

archaeology.t: Bedouin tents of black goat hair continue an ancient pattern.
Andrei Rublev painted the three visitors around a table about 1411-1425 (Tretyakov Gallery, Moscow).

overview.discussion: Abraham kept asking, “Suppose ten are found there?” (v.32). For whom am I willing to plead with God that persistently?
overview.book: The book of Genesis · 50 chapters (1-25 in the app so far). Beginnings: creation, the fall, the flood and the nations, then God’s promise to Abraham and his family.
overview.author: Moses, by tradition

biblePlaces.name: Sodom and Gomorrah (site debated; south end of the Dead Sea proposed)

historicalImage.caption: Abraham Serving the Three Angels, by Rembrandt (1646, private collection). The visitors eat under the tree while Sarah listens at the door of the tent (Genesis 18:8-10).

currentImage.caption: The traditional site of Mamre near Hebron (Ramat el-Khalil). “The LORD appeared to Abraham by the Oaks of Mamre in the heat of the day, while he was sitting at the entrance of his tent” (Genesis 18:1). Herod walled the site, and Constantine built a church there in the 4th century.
